meta.title: Lanchester fixed reading list (open primary sources beyond the textbooks)
meta.curriculum: round3/final/F_curriculum.json (Lanchester modules incl. new M6.12, M7.4, M7.10, M8.8, M8.9, M9.9, M13.23, M14.1-M14.5)
meta.hours_note: Estimated focused-reading hours for the "focus" portions only, not the whole document.
meta.tiers: core = read when the host module is taught; optional = read only if the module raises the question or for an article on it
excluded_not_open: IISS The Military Balance (paywalled; use a library copy for OOB numbers, cite with year)
Hughes 1995 NRL salvo paper (paywalled; NPS-OR-93-001 used instead)
Mearsheimer 1989 / Epstein 3:1 debate (International Security, paywalled; B14 covers it)
Fleeman NATO RTO-EN-018 lecture notes (no open full text found; Fleeman B13 is in the library)
rough: RM items with link_status "rough" (Conflict Armament Research, CRS Red Sea Insight) point to a landing/search page
Fetter & Wright 2025 and OEG-51 links timed out from the sandbox
Year/edition of annual series (DOT&E, GAO WSAA, SWF, CSIS, DoD China) should be refreshed to the latest edition when the module is taught

items.title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
items.why: The source of channel capacity C = B log2(1+S/N); every 'jam-resistant link' or 'bandwidth vs range' claim is bounded by it.
items.focus: Part I sec. 1-2 for the idea of information; Part IV (continuous channel) sec. 24-25 for the capacity theorem and the power-limited regime. Skip the proofs.

items.title: A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems
items.why: The original Kalman filter; tracking (M2.15), INS/GNSS integration (M5.8) and guidance filters all rest on it.
items.focus: Sections 1-3 (problem statement, orthogonal projection) and the summary table of the filter equations; read for where the Gaussian/linear assumptions enter.

items.title: Feedback Systems: An Introduction for Scientists and Engineers
items.authors: K. J. Astrom, R. M. Murray
items.link_status: timeout from sandbox; URL from publisher/search result, verify in a browser
items.why: Free, rigorous control text at exactly the 'why loops behave this way' level; fills gaps before autopilots (M6.2) and guidance loops.
items.focus: Ch.1 (feedback principles), ch.9-10 (loop transfer function, Nyquist, gain/phase margin). Read only where M0.7 feels thin.

items.title: The Development of Phased-Array Radar Technology
items.authors: A. J. Fenn, D. H. Temme, W. P. Delaney, W. E. Courtney
items.why: 40 years of array history from the lab that built many of them; shows why cost per T/R module, not physics, decided adoption.
items.focus: Sections on element cost, solid-state T/R modules and the cost curve; the BMD and ATC case histories.

items.title: ITU-R P.525 (free-space attenuation) and P.676 (attenuation by atmospheric gases)
items.why: The authoritative curves for atmospheric loss vs frequency; lets you check any 'mmWave/60 GHz' or 'W-band seeker' range claim yourself.
items.focus: P.676 Annex 2 (approximate method) and its attenuation-vs-frequency figure; P.525 is 4 pages (https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-P.525/en). Note the 22 GHz and 60 GHz lines.

items.title: ITU-R P.838 (rain attenuation) and P.526 (propagation by diffraction)
items.why: Rain fade and knife-edge diffraction are the two most-ignored terms in link and low-altitude radar budgets.
items.focus: P.838: the k*R^alpha model and coefficient table; P.526 (https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-P.526/en) sec. 4 single knife-edge.

items.title: Introduction to Radar Systems (lecture series, slides)
items.why: Lincoln Lab's own course: compact, numerically grounded slides that map 1:1 to M2.1-M2.16; ideal second view of each topic.
items.focus: Lectures on the radar equation, detection, CFAR, Doppler/MTI, tracking. Use as a 20-minute check per module, not cover to cover.

items.title: Electronic Warfare and Radar Systems Engineering Handbook (4th ed., NAWCWD TP 8347)
items.authors: Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division
items.why: The US Navy's own 'back of the envelope' handbook for radar and EW; the best open source of rule-of-thumb formulas and numbers.
items.focus: Sections 4 (radar equations), 4-4 (jamming-to-signal), 4-8/4-11 (burn-through), 5 (radar cross section), 2 (dB math). Keep as a lookup reference.

items.title: Probability of Detection for Fluctuating Targets (RM-1217)
items.why: Defines Swerling cases I-IV; explains why a fluctuating target costs 5-10 dB at high Pd, a common error in public range estimates.
items.focus: Case definitions and the comparison figure of required SNR vs Pd for steady vs fluctuating targets.

items.title: A Statistical Theory of Target Detection by Pulsed Radar (RM-754)
items.why: The origin of Pd/Pfa curves and integration gain; every detection-range number descends from it.
items.focus: Introduction and the definitions of false-alarm number and detection probability; the integration-loss discussion. Skip the tables.

items.title: Performance Limits for Synthetic Aperture Radar, 2nd ed. (SAND2006-0821)
items.link_status: timeout from sandbox; URL from publisher/search result, verify in a browser
items.why: Physics limits on SAR resolution, area rate and noise-equivalent sigma-zero; lets you judge commercial and military SAR claims (also M2.25, M13.11).
items.focus: The SNR/area-coverage-rate equations and the weather/frequency band discussion; the summary of fundamental limits.

items.title: The Targeting Task Performance (TTP) Metric: A New Model for Predicting Target Acquisition Performance
items.why: The Army's replacement for the Johnson criteria; the basis of every 'detect/recognize/identify at X km' claim for thermal sights and drone cameras.
items.focus: Ch.1-2 (Johnson criteria and why they fail for sampled imagers), the TTP definition, and the V50 tables. Skip the experiment appendices.

items.title: Search and Screening (OEG Report No. 56)
items.why: Founding text of search theory: sweep width, random-search formula, inverse-cube law; also host for ASW search in M10.3.
items.focus: Ch.1-3 (contacts, sweep width, random search 1 - exp(-WL/A)) and ch.7 (optimal distribution of effort). OCR is rough; read the formulas carefully.

items.title: Search for the Wreckage of Air France Flight AF 447
items.authors: L. D. Stone, C. M. Keller, T. M. Kratzke, J. P. Strumpfer
items.why: Modern Bayesian search theory applied to a real case: shows how combining priors and failed searches found the wreck in a week.
items.focus: Sections 2-4: the prior, the likelihood of failed searches, and the posterior map. Note how the analysts handled a possibly failed beacon.

items.title: Department of Defense Directed Energy Weapons: Background and Issues for Congress (R46925)
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: Neutral summary of HEL and HPM programs with power levels and funding; the base for any laser C-UAS / ship-defense claim.
items.focus: The program tables (power class, platform) and the 'issues' section on dwell time, atmospherics and magazine depth.

items.title: Preliminary Lessons in Conventional Warfighting from Russia's Invasion of Ukraine: February-July 2022
items.authors: M. Zabrodskyi, J. Watling, O. Danylyuk, N. Reynolds
items.why: First open data-rich analysis of the war from inside Ukrainian staffs: EW effects on drones and comms, artillery dominance, air defense.
items.focus: The sections on electronic warfare, air defense and artillery/ISR; note which numbers come from Ukrainian sources.

items.title: Statistical Theory of Passive Location Systems
items.why: The standard derivation of DF and TDOA location accuracy (CEP, GDOP); lets you check claims about how fast SIGINT can locate an emitter.
items.focus: Sections on the triangulation (DF) estimator, hyperbolic (TDOA) location and the CEP approximation. Scan is rough; the IEEE AES-20(2) 1984 version is cleaner.

items.title: Winning the Airwaves: Regaining America's Dominance in the Electromagnetic Spectrum
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: Clear statement of the 'low-signature + passive + distributed' shift in EW thinking; good background for EP and LPI.
items.focus: Ch.2 (the competition between sensors and countermeasures) and ch.3 (proposed concepts). Treat the program advocacy critically.

items.title: Above Us Only Stars: Exposing GPS Spoofing in Russia and Syria
items.why: How AIS and GNSS receiver data exposed nearly 10,000 spoofing incidents; a model of OSINT method applied to EW (also M14.4).
items.focus: Methodology section (how spoofing is detected from AIS tracks), and the case studies near Russian leadership sites and Khmeimim.

items.title: EASA Safety Information Bulletin 2022-02R3: GNSS Outages and Alterations
items.why: Official regulator acknowledgment of wide GNSS jamming/spoofing around the Baltic, Black Sea and Middle East; shows the civil spillover.
items.focus: The affected-area list and recommended crew actions.

items.title: GPS Standard Positioning Service (SPS) Performance Standard, 5th ed.
items.why: The official, committed numbers (signal-in-space URE, availability, accuracy); the yardstick against which every degraded-GPS claim is measured.
items.focus: Sec. 3.4-3.8 (SIS accuracy, integrity, continuity, availability) and the position-domain accuracy standards. Compare committed vs typical performance.

items.title: Analyzing a More Resilient National Positioning, Navigation, and Timing Capability (RR-2970)
items.why: Systematic comparison of alt-PNT options (eLoran, LEO PNT, terrestrial, quantum) on coverage, accuracy and cost.
items.focus: The options comparison table and the summary; skip the stakeholder sections.

items.title: Basic Principles of Homing Guidance; Modern Homing Missile Guidance Theory and Techniques
items.authors: N. F. Palumbo, R. A. Blauwkamp, J. M. Lloyd
items.why: The clearest open treatment of PN, miss distance, zero-effort miss and optimal guidance, from the lab that designs Standard Missile guidance.
items.focus: Palumbo 'Basic Principles' (PN derivation, ZEM, adjoint miss-distance) and 'Modern Homing...' (https://jhuapl.edu/sites/default/files/2024-09/29-01-Palumbo_Homing.pdf). Also skim the issue's seeker and guidance-filter articles for M6.6.

items.title: Precision-Guided Munitions: Background and Issues for Congress (R45996)
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: Inventory, guidance types (GPS/INS, laser, multimode) and procurement numbers of US PGMs; numbers for stockpile and weapon-delivery lessons.
items.focus: The guidance-type summary and the procurement tables.

items.title: A Simple Model for Calculating Ballistic Missile Defense Effectiveness
items.why: The standard open model linking SSPK, shoot-look-shoot, reliability and leakage to interceptor inventory; read before M7.1-M7.4.
items.focus: Sections 2-4 (the probability model, SLS, imperfect discrimination) and the NMD/TMD worked examples. Re-derive one example by hand.

items.title: An Analysis of the North Korean Nodong Missile
items.why: Model example of reverse-engineering a missile from open data (clustered Scud engines, mass fractions, range, CEP); the method you need for any new missile.
items.focus: The modeling method: staging, burn time, drag, range-payload curve and CEP estimate; redo the rocket-equation step yourself.

items.title: Modeling the Performance of Hypersonic Boost-Glide Missiles
items.why: Physics-based critique showing glide vehicles lose speed to drag and stay IR-bright; judgment-changing for 'unstoppable hypersonic' claims.
items.focus: The trajectory model, the speed/range comparison with ballistic missiles, and the IR detectability section. Then read the Candler-Leyva comment and the authors' reply (SGS 31, 2023).

items.title: U.S. Hypersonic Weapons and Alternatives
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: Cost-effectiveness comparison of hypersonic vs ballistic and cruise alternatives: ~1/3 more cost per missile for a capability many missions do not need.
items.focus: Summary, the cost comparison (300 missiles, 20 years), and the mission-by-mission analysis of when speed matters.

items.title: National Cruise Missile Defense: Issues and Alternatives
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: Shows the geometry problem of low-flying cruise missiles (radar horizon, area to cover) and its cost: $75-465 billion options.
items.focus: The radar-horizon and coverage discussion and the cost-of-options table.

items.title: CSIS Missile Threat: missile database
items.why: Open, sourced reference sheets (range, payload, propulsion, status) for most ballistic and cruise missiles; the quick lookup for design-trade sanity checks.
items.focus: Use per missile when a lesson cites one; check the sources at the bottom of each sheet before quoting.

items.title: The Russian Air War and Ukrainian Requirements for Air Defence
items.authors: J. Bronk, N. Reynolds, J. Watling
items.why: How ground-based air defense denied Russia air superiority and how Russia adapted (low flight, stand-off, Shaheds); AMD MOEs in a real war.
items.focus: Sections on SEAD failure, Russian low-altitude tactics, and Ukrainian GBAD needs by threat class.

items.title: Winning the Salvo Competition: Rebalancing America's Air and Missile Defenses
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: Frames AMD as a salvo/magazine and cost-exchange competition; the conceptual bridge between M7.4 and M14.1.
items.focus: Ch.2 (salvo competition and cost exchange), ch.3 (layered defense options: HPM, EW, guns). Compare numbers with Red Sea expenditures.

items.title: Cost and Value in Air and Missile Defense Intercepts
items.why: Argues that interceptor-vs-threat cost ratios mislead; the right comparison is value defended and cost of the alternative. Uses the Red Sea case.
items.focus: The full piece; write down the three cost metrics it distinguishes.

items.title: Missile defense in the 2024 Iranian attacks on Israel (Washington Quarterly 48:2)
items.link_status: timeout from sandbox; URL from publisher/search result, verify in a browser
items.why: A physicist's analysis of the April/October 2024 salvos: what the interception claims mean, the denominator problem, interceptor use.
items.focus: Sections on the salvo composition, the claimed intercept rates and how to read them. [link timed out from the sandbox; verify in a browser]

items.title: Making Sense of Ballistic Missile Defense: An Assessment of Concepts and Systems for U.S. Boost-Phase Missile Defense in Comparison to Other Alternatives
items.why: The most authoritative open technical assessment of BMD: boost-phase infeasibility, the role of radar discrimination, shoot-look-shoot economics.
items.focus: Summary; ch.2 (boost-phase timelines); ch.5 (radar and discrimination); appendices on the 'shoot-look-shoot' cost model.

items.title: History and the Current Status of the Russian Early-Warning System
items.why: Detailed open history of Russian EW radars and satellites, with coverage gaps; the reference case for early-warning architecture and its strategic stakes.
items.focus: Sections on the radar network coverage and the Oko/US-KS satellite system; the coverage maps.

items.title: Mosaic Warfare: Exploiting Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Systems to Implement Decision-Centric Operations
items.authors: B. Clark, D. Patt, H. Schramm
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: The intellectual source of 'kill webs' and decision-centric warfare behind JADC2; know it to critique it.
items.focus: Ch.1-3: the argument against monolithic kill chains, the composability idea, and the wargame evidence offered (judge its strength).

items.title: Joint All-Domain Command and Control (JADC2) (R46725)
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: Neutral summary of what JADC2 is, its service programs and its open problems (data standards, EW, cost).
items.focus: Background and 'issues for Congress'.

items.title: Technical Debate over Patriot Performance in the Gulf War
items.authors: J. D. Sullivan, D. Fenstermacher, D. Fetter, R. Ruggiero, A. Shanks
items.why: The classic case of intercept claims collapsing under evidence (claims of ~80% vs evidence of few warhead kills); the template for reading every later claim.
items.focus: How 'intercept' was defined, what video evidence can and cannot show, and the role of the scoring criteria.

items.title: Operation Desert Storm: Data Does Not Exist to Conclusively Say How Well Patriot Performed (NSIAD-92-340)
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: GAO on why the Army's Patriot claims could not be verified; a short, sharp lesson in test-evidence standards.
items.focus: Results in brief and the section on the Army's evidence categories.

items.title: DOT&E Annual Report (latest: FY2025, March 2026): BMDS and AMD program sections
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: The only open source that grades major weapons against operational test evidence; teaches what 'operationally effective and suitable' means in practice.
items.focus: The Missile Defense Agency (BMDS/GMD/THAAD/Aegis) sections and 2-3 programs you study (e.g., IBCS, SM-6, F-35). Read the 'Assessment' paragraphs. Older years were briefly removed from the site in 2026; archived copies via USNI News.

items.title: Patriot Missile Defense: Software Problem Led to System Failure at Dhahran (IMTEC-92-26)
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: The clock-drift range-gate error (0.34 s after 100 h) that killed 28 soldiers; the classic example of an operational-use assumption breaking a system.
items.focus: The technical explanation of the timing error and the range-gate shift.

items.title: Statistics, Testing, and Defense Acquisition: New Approaches and Methodological Improvements
items.why: How few test shots support (or don't) a reliability claim; the open source for the 'few-shot statistics' item in M7.10.
items.focus: Ch.3 (statistical issues in operational testing) and the success-run/confidence discussion.

items.title: Gulf War Air Power Survey, Vol. II: Operations and Effects and Effectiveness
items.authors: E. A. Cohen (dir.), T. A. Keaney et al.
items.why: The most rigorous open air-campaign effectiveness study: Scud hunt failure, BDA problems, PGM vs unguided effects.
items.focus: Part II 'Effects and Effectiveness': the Scud-hunt chapter and the strategic-target chapters; the Summary Report (Keaney & Cohen) gives the overview.

items.title: Trends in Air-to-Air Combat: Implications for Future Air Superiority
items.link_status: exists; site blocks automated fetch (HTTP 403); title/ID confirmed by web search or known catalog
items.why: Data on 1965-2010 air-to-air kills: share of BVR kills, role of situational awareness, decline of dogfights. Changes intuition from Top Gun to sensors.
items.focus: The kill-data charts (WVR vs BVR, by war) and the argument on range/endurance; check how 'kills' were counted.

items.title: Report of the Defense Science Board Task Force on Patriot System Performance: Report Summary
items.why: 2003 Patriot fratricides (Tornado, F/A-18): how IFF, ROE and automation interacted; the canonical combat-ID lesson.
items.focus: The whole summary (short): combat-ID findings and the automation/operator-trust discussion.

items.title: Air Power Survey data on losses: see GWAPS Vol. V Statistical Compendium

items.title: Airbase Vulnerability to Conventional Cruise-Missile and Ballistic-Missile Attacks (MR-1028)
items.why: The classic quantitative model of how many missiles close an airbase (submunitions vs parked aircraft, runway cuts).
items.focus: The attack model (CEP, submunition patterns, aircraft on ramps) and the results tables; then ask how Ukraine 2022-25 airbase strikes compare.

items.title: Sortie Generation Capacity of Embarked Airwings (CRM 98-111)
items.why: Measured carrier surge and sustained sortie rates and their limits (deck cycle, maintenance, aircrew); the empirical base for 'sorties per day'.
items.focus: The constraints analysis (airframe, pilots, turnaround) and the surge-vs-sustained results.

items.title: DoD Directive 3000.09: Autonomy in Weapon Systems (2023)

items.title: Autonomous Weapons and Operational Risk
items.why: Systems-safety view of autonomy: failure modes, coupling, why fratricide risk scales; ties to the Patriot 2003 case.

items.title: Evolution Not Revolution: Drone Warfare in Russia's 2022 Invasion of Ukraine
items.why: Balanced, data-based assessment of drones in Ukraine: what changed, what did not, loss rates to EW, the adaptation cycle.

items.title: Mass Precision Strike: Designing UAV Complexes for Land Forces
items.why: Turns Ukraine experience into force-design numbers: drones per target, hit rates, EW attrition, the mix of recon, strike and FPV.

items.why: The 2020 war as a preview: TB2 and loitering munitions against unadapted air defenses; what was really new and what was poor Armenian AD.

items.title: ESA Space Environment Report 2025
items.why: Authoritative debris and traffic statistics (objects tracked, fragmentation events, compliance); needed for any ASAT-debris argument.
items.focus: Executive summary and the trends charts (object counts by orbit, fragmentations).

items.title: National Imagery Interpretability Rating Scale (NIIRS)

items.title: The Recent Large Reduction in Space Launch Cost (ICES-2018-81)
items.why: Launch cost per kg history (factor ~20 fall); a premise behind proliferated constellations and responsive space.

items.title: State-of-the-Art of Small Spacecraft Technology
items.authors: NASA Small Spacecraft Systems Virtual Institute

items.title: Global Counterspace Capabilities: An Open Source Assessment (annual)
items.why: The reference open assessment of counterspace capabilities by country and type (DA-ASAT, co-orbital, EW, DE, cyber), with evidence ratings.

items.title: Space Threat Assessment (annual; 2025 and 2026 eds.)
items.authors: C. Swope, K. Bingen, M. Young et al.
items.why: Annual update of counterspace developments, including the Ukraine war's GNSS/SATCOM jamming and Russian nuclear ASAT concerns.

items.title: A History of Anti-Satellite Programs
items.why: Short history of US/Soviet/Chinese ASAT programs and tests, including the 2007 debris event; the background for the SWF/CSIS annuals.

items.title: Aircraft in Warfare: The Dawn of the Fourth Arm
items.why: The source of the linear and N-square laws; reading it shows how modest and conditional the original claims were.
items.focus: Chapters V and VI (the N-square law, its derivation and the Nelson/Trafalgar illustration).

items.title: The Base of Sand Problem: A White Paper on the State of Military Combat Modeling (N-3148)
items.why: The canonical critique of combat models: attrition rules without empirical base; what a model can and cannot be evidence for. Judgment-changing.

items.title: Why Wargaming Works
items.authors: P. P. Perla, E. D. McGrady
items.why: The best short account of what wargames produce (insight, not prediction); needed to judge CSIS/RAND wargame claims.
items.focus: Whole article; list the kinds of claims a wargame can legitimately support.

items.title: Decision in Battle: Breakpoint Hypotheses and Engagement Termination Data (R-772)

items.focus: The breakpoint hypotheses and the data tests; note how weak the casualty-fraction rule is.
